entries.b963158a84deae00044c7f3e670e4930b9c5285d: <div sID="gen20681" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Zeph.3" sID="Zeph.3"/> <div eID="gen20681" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20682" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen20683" type="x-p"/> We now return to Jerusalem, and must again hear what God has to say to her, I. By way of reproof and threatening, for the abundance of wickedness that was found in her, of which divers instances are given, with the aggravations of them, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.1-Zeph.3.7">ver. 1-7</reference>. II. By way of promise of mercy and grace, which God had yet in reserve for them. Two general heads of promises here are:—1. That God would bring in a glorious work of reformation among them, cleanse them from their sins, and bring them home to himself; many promises of this kind here are, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13">ver. 8-13</reference>. 2. That he would bring about a glorious work of salvation for them, when he had thus prepared them for it, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.14-Zeph.3.20">ver. 14-20</reference>. Thus the "Redeemer shall come to Zion," and to clear his own way, shall "turn away ungodliness from Jacob." These promises were to have their full accomplishment in gospel-times and gospel-graces.
entries.b0df6d6e4d866953bfe6b5b8d144069855892910: <div eID="gen20683" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen20682" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Depravity of Jerusalem. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 612.)</title> <div sID="gen20684" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city! <hi type="super">2</hi> She obeyed not the voice; she received not correction; she trusted not in the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> ; she drew not near to her God. <hi type="super">3</hi> Her princes within her <hi type="italic">are</hi> roaring lions; her judges <hi type="italic">are</hi> evening wolves; they gnaw not the bones till the morrow. <hi type="super">4</hi> Her prophets <hi type="italic">are</hi> light <hi type="italic">and</hi> treacherous persons: her priests have polluted the sanctuary, they have done violence to the law. <hi type="super">5</hi> The just <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the midst thereof; he will not do iniquity: every morning doth he bring his judgment to light, he faileth not; but the unjust knoweth no shame. <hi type="super">6</hi> I have cut off the nations: their towers are desolate; I made their streets waste, that none passeth by: their cities are destroyed, so that there is no man, that there is none inhabitant. <hi type="super">7</hi> I said, Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt receive instruction; so their dwelling should not be cut off, howsoever I punished them: but they rose early, <hi type="italic">and</hi> corrupted all their doings. <div eID="gen20684" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20685" type="x-p"/> One would wonder that Jerusalem, the holy city, where God was known, and his name was great, should be the city of which this black character is here given, that a place which enjoyed such abundance of the means of grace should become so very corrupt and vicious, and that God should permit it to be so; yet so it is, to show that <hi type="italic">the law made nothing perfect;</hi> but if this be the true character of Jerusalem, as no doubt it is (for God's judgments will make none worse than they are), it is no wonder that the prophet begins with <hi type="italic">woe to her.</hi> For the holy God hates sin in those that are nearest to him, nay, in them he hates it most. A sinful state is, and will be, a woeful state. <div eID="gen20685" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20686" type="x-p"/> I. Here is a very bad character given of the city in general. How has the faithful city become a harlot! 1. She shames herself; she is <hi type="italic">filthy and polluted</hi> (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.1">v. 1</reference>), has made herself <hi type="italic">infamous</hi> (so some read it), <hi type="italic">the gluttonous</hi> city (so the margin), always cramming, and making provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts of it. Sin is the filthiness and pollution of persons and places, and makes them odious in the sight of the holy God. 2. She wrongs her neighbours and inhabitants; she is <hi type="italic">the oppressing city.</hi> Never any place had <hi type="italic">statutes and judgments so righteous</hi> as this city had, and yet, in the administration of the government, never was more unrighteousness. 3. She is very provoking to her God, and in every respect walks contrary to him, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.2">v. 2</reference>. He had given his law, and spoken to her by his servants the prophets, telling her what was the good she should do and what the evil she should avoid; but <hi type="italic">she obeyed not his voice,</hi> nor made conscience of doing as he commanded her, in any thing. He had taken her under an excellent discipline, both of the word and of the rod; but she did not receive the instruction of the one nor the correction of the other, did not submit to God's will nor answer his end in either. He encouraged her to depend upon him, and his power and promise, for deliverance from evil and supply with good; but she <hi type="italic">trusted not in the Lord;</hi> her confidence was placed in her alliances with the nations more than in her covenant with God. He gave her tokens of his presence, and instituted ordinances of communion for her with himself; but she <hi type="italic">drew not near to her God,</hi> did not meet him where he appointed and where he promised to meet her. She stood at a distance, and <hi type="italic">said to the Almighty, Depart.</hi> <div eID="gen20686" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20687" type="x-p"/> II. Here is a very bad character of the leading men in it; those that should by their influence suppress vice and profaneness there are the great patterns and patrons of wickedness, and those that should be her physicians are really her worst disease. 1. <hi type="italic">Her princes are</hi> ravenous and barbarous as <hi type="italic">roaring lions</hi> that make a prey of all about them, and they are universally feared and hated; they use their power for destruction, and not for edification. 2. <hi type="italic">Her judges,</hi> who should be the protectors of injured innocence, <hi type="italic">are evening wolves,</hi> rapacious and greedy, and their cruelty and covetousness both insatiable: <hi type="italic">They gnaw not the bones till the morrow;</hi> they take so much delight and pleasure in cruelty and oppression that when they have devoured a good man they reserve the bones, as it were, for a sweet morsel, to be gnawed the next morning, <reference osisRef="Job.31.31">Job xxxi. 31</reference>. 3. <hi type="italic">Her prophets,</hi> who pretend to be special messengers from heaven to them, <hi type="italic">are light and treacherous persons,</hi> fanciful, and of a vain imagination, frothy and airy, and of a loose conversation, men of no consistency with themselves, in whom one can put no confidence. They were so given to bantering that it was hard to say when they were serious. Their pretended prophecies were all a sham, and they secretly laughed at those that were deluded by them. 4. <hi type="italic">Her priests,</hi> who are teachers by office and have the charge of the holy things, are false to their trust and betray it. They were to preserve the purity of the <hi type="italic">sanctuary,</hi> but they did themselves <hi type="italic">pollute</hi> it, and the sacred offices of it, which they were to attend upon—such priests as Hophni and Phinehas, who by their wicked lives <hi type="italic">made the sacrifices of the Lord to be abhorred.</hi> They were to expound and apply <hi type="italic">the law,</hi> and to judge according to it; but, in their explications and applications of it, they <hi type="italic">did violence to the law;</hi> they corrupted the sense of it, and perverted it to the patronising of that which was directly contrary to it. By forced constructions, they made the law to speak what they pleased, to serve a turn, and so, in effect, <hi type="italic">made void the law.</hi> <div eID="gen20687" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20688" type="x-p"/> III. We have here the aggravations of this general corruption of all orders and degrees of men in Jerusalem. <div eID="gen20688" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20689" type="x-p"/> 1. They had the tokens of God's presence among them, and all the advantages that could be of knowing his will, with the strongest inducements possible to do it, and yet they persisted in their disobedience, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.5">v. 5</reference>. (1.) They had the honour and privilege of the Shechinah, God's dwelling in their land, so as he dwelt not with any other people: "<hi type="italic">The just Lord is in the midst of thee,</hi> to take cognizance of all thou doest amiss and give countenance to all thou doest well; he is in the midst of thee as a holy God, and therefore thy pollutions are the more offensive, <reference osisRef="Deut.23.14">Deut. xxiii. 14</reference>. He is in the midst of you as a just God, and therefore will punish the affronts you put upon him, and the wrongs and injuries you do to one another." (2.) They had God's own example set before them, in the discovery he made of himself to them, that they might conform to it: "<hi type="italic">He will not do iniquity,</hi> and therefore you should not;" for this was the great rule of their institution, "<hi type="italic">Be you holy, for I am holy.</hi> God will be true to you; be not you then false to him." (3.) He sent to them his prophets, rising up early and sending them: <hi type="italic">Every morning he brings his judgment to light,</hi> as duly as the morning comes; <hi type="italic">he fails not.</hi> He shows them plainly what the good is which he requires of them, and puts them in mind of it; he <hi type="italic">wakens morning by morning</hi> (<reference osisRef="Isa.50.4">Isa. l. 4</reference>), wakens his prophets with the rising sun, to bring to light the things which belong to their peace. So that, upon the whole matter, what more could have been done to his vineyard, to make it fruitful? <reference osisRef="Isa.5.4">Isa. v. 4</reference>. And yet, after all, <hi type="italic">the unjust know no shame;</hi> those that have been unjust are unjust still, and are not ashamed of their unrighteousness, <hi type="italic">neither can they blush.</hi> If they had any sense of honour, any shame left in them, they would not go so directly contrary to their profession and to the instructions given them. But those that are past shame are past cure. <div eID="gen20689" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20690" type="x-p"/> 2. God had set before their eyes some remarkable monuments of his justice, which were designed for warning to them (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.6">v. 6</reference>): <hi type="italic">I have cut off the nations,</hi> the seven nations of Canaan, which the land spewed out for their wickedness, upon which they had this caution given them, to take heed lest it <hi type="italic">spew them out also,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.18.28">Lev. xviii. 28</reference>. Or it may refer to some of the neighbouring nations that were made desolate for their wickedness, especially to the nations of Israel, the ten tribes. <hi type="italic">Their towers were desolate,</hi> their high towers, their strong towers, their pride and power broken; their <hi type="italic">streets were wasted,</hi> so that none passed along through them; <hi type="italic">their cities</hi> were <hi type="italic">destroyed</hi> and laid in ruins; <hi type="italic">no man</hi> was to be found in them, <hi type="italic">no inhabitant,</hi> all were slain or carried into captivity. The enemies did it, but God avows it: <hi type="italic">I cut them off,</hi> says he. And God designed this for an admonition to Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Ezek.23.9">Ezek. xxiii. 9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.23.11">11</reference>): "<hi type="italic">I said, Surely thou wilt fear me;</hi> surely these judgments upon others will deter thee from the like wicked practices; <hi type="italic">surely thou wilt receive instruction</hi> by these providences; it ought to be expected that thou wouldst not continue to sin like the nations when thou seest the ruin which their sin brought upon them." They could not but see their own house in danger when their neighbour's was on fire; and, when we are frightened, God should be feared. <div eID="gen20690" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20691" type="x-p"/> 3. He had set before them life and death, good and evil, both in his word and in his providence. (1.) He had assured them of the continuance of their prosperity if they would fear him and receive instruction, for so <hi type="italic">their dwelling would not be cut off</hi> as their neighbour's was; if they took the warning given them, and reformed, what was past should be pardoned, and their tranquility lengthened out. (2.) He had made them feel the smart of the rod, though he reprieved them from the sword: <hi type="italic">Howsoever I punished them,</hi> that, being chastened, they might not be condemned. Such various methods did God take with them, to reclaim them, but all in vain; they were not won upon by gentle methods, nor had severe ones any effect, for <hi type="italic">they rose early, and corrupted all their doings;</hi> they were more resolute and eager in their wicked courses than ever, more studious and solicitous in making provision for their lusts, and let slip no opportunity for the gratification of them. God <hi type="italic">rose up early,</hi> to send them his <hi type="italic">prophets,</hi> to reduce and reclaim them, but they were <hi type="italic">up before him,</hi> to shut and bolt the door against them. Their wickedness was universal: <hi type="italic">All their doings</hi> were corrupted; and it was all owing to themselves; they could not lay the blame upon the tempter, but they alone must bear it; they themselves wilfully and designedly <hi type="italic">corrupted all their doings;</hi> for <hi type="italic">every man is tempted when he is drawn aside of his own lust and enticed.</hi>
entries.c0ff826e730c2905a00a2adc96537e3da49ab435: <div eID="gen20691" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Judgment and Mercy; Promises of Mercy. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 612.)</title> <div sID="gen20692" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">8</hi> Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , until the day that I rise up to the prey: for my determination <hi type="italic">is</hi> to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them mine indignation, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all my fierce anger: for all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy. <hi type="super">9</hi> For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , to serve him with one consent. <hi type="super">10</hi> From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring mine offering. <hi type="super">11</hi> In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain. <hi type="super">12</hi> I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">13</hi> The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make <hi type="italic">them</hi> afraid. <div eID="gen20692" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20693" type="x-p"/> Things looked very bad with Jerusalem in the <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.1-Zeph.3.7">foregoing verses</reference>; she has got into a very bad name, and seems to be incorrigible, incurable, mercy-proof and judgment-proof. Now one would think it should follow, Therefore expect no other but that she should be utterly abandoned and rejected as <hi type="italic">reprobate silver;</hi> since they will not be wrought upon by prophets or providences, let them be made a desolation as their neighbours have been. But behold and wonder at the riches of divine grace, which takes occasion from man's badness to appear so much the more illustrious. They still grew worse and worse, <hi type="italic">therefore wait you upon me, saith the Lord,</hi> <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.8">v. 8</reference>. "Since the <hi type="italic">law,</hi> it seems, will <hi type="italic">make nothing perfect,</hi> the <hi type="italic">bringing in of a better hope shall.</hi> Let those that lament the corruptions of the church <hi type="italic">wait upon God,</hi> till he send his Son into the world, to <hi type="italic">save his people from their sins,</hi> till he send his gospel to reform and refine his church, and to purify to himself a peculiar people both of Jews and Gentiles." And there were those who, according to this direction and encouragement, <hi type="italic">waited for redemption,</hi> for this redemption in Jerusalem; and long-looked-for came at last, <reference osisRef="Luke.2.38">Luke ii. 38</reference>. <hi type="italic">For judgment</hi> Christ will <hi type="italic">come into this world,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.9.39">John ix. 39</reference>. <div eID="gen20693" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20694" type="x-p"/> I. To avenge what has been done amiss against his church, to bring down and destroy the enemies of it, its spiritual enemies, of which the destruction of Babylon, and other oppressors of God's people, in the Old-Testament times, was a type, and would be a happy presage. He will <hi type="italic">rise up to the prey,</hi> to <hi type="italic">lead captivity captive</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.67.18">Ps. lxvii. 18</reference>), to conquer and spoil the powers of darkness, and the powers on earth that set themselves <hi type="italic">against the Lord and his anointed;</hi> he will <hi type="italic">break them with a rod of iron</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.5 Ps.2.9 Ps.11.5-Ps.11.6">Ps. ii. 5, 9; xi. 5, 6</reference>); his <hi type="italic">determination is to gather the nations</hi> and to <hi type="italic">assemble the kingdoms.</hi> By the gospel of Christ preached to every creature all nations are summoned, as it were, to appear in a body before the Lord Jesus, who is about to set up his kingdom in the world. But, since the greatest part of mankind will not obey the summons, he will <hi type="italic">pour upon them his indignation,</hi> for he that <hi type="italic">believes not is condemned already.</hi> At the time of the setting up of the kingdom of the Messiah, there shall be on earth <hi type="italic">distress of nations with perplexity</hi> (<reference osisRef="Luke.21.25">Luke xxi. 25</reference>), <hi type="italic">great tribulation,</hi> such as <hi type="italic">never was, nor ever shall be,</hi> <reference osisRef="Matt.24.21">Matt. xxiv. 21</reference>. Then God pours upon the nations his indignation, even <hi type="italic">all his fierce anger,</hi> for their indignation and fierce anger against the Messiah and his kingdom, <reference osisRef="Ps.2.1-Ps.2.2">Ps. ii. 1, 2</reference>. Then <hi type="italic">all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of his jealousy;</hi> both Jews and Gentiles shall be reckoned with for their enmity to the gospel. Principalities and powers shall be spoiled, and <hi type="italic">made a show of openly,</hi> and the victorious Redeemer shall triumph over them. The end of those that continue to be of the earth, and to <hi type="italic">mind earthly things,</hi> after God has set up the <hi type="italic">kingdom of heaven</hi> among men, <hi type="italic">shall be destruction</hi> (<reference osisRef="Phil.3.19">Phil. iii. 19</reference>); they shall be <hi type="italic">devoured with the fire of God's jealousy.</hi> <div eID="gen20694" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20695" type="x-p"/> II. To amend what he finds amiss in his church. When God intends the restoration of Israel, and the revival of their peace and prosperity, he makes way for the accomplishment of his purpose by their reformation and the revival of their virtue and piety; for this is God's method, both with particular persons and with communities, first to make them holy and then to make them happy. These promises were in part accomplished after the return of the Jews out of Babylon, when by their captivity they were thoroughly cured of their idolatry; and this was all the fruit, even the taking away of sin. But they look further, to the blessed effects of the gospel and the grace of it, to those <hi type="italic">times of reformation</hi> in which we live, <reference osisRef="Heb.9.10">Heb. ix. 10</reference>. <div eID="gen20695" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20696" type="x-p"/> 1. It is promised that there shall be a reformation in men's discourse, which had been generally corrupt, but should now be with grace seasoned with salt (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.9">v. 9</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Then will I turn to the people a pure language;</hi> I will turn the people to such a language from that <hi type="italic">evil communication</hi> which has almost ruined all <hi type="italic">good manners</hi> among them." Note, Converting grace refines the language, not by making the phrases witty, but the substance wise. Among the Jews, after the captivity, there needed a reformation of the dialect, for they had mingled the language of Canaan with that of Ashdod (<reference osisRef="Neh.13.24">Neh. xiii. 24</reference>), and that grievance shall be redressed. But that is not all: their language shall be purified from all profaneness, filthiness, and falsehood. I will turn them to a <hi type="italic">choice language</hi> (so some read it); they shall not speak rashly, but with caution and deliberation; they shall <hi type="italic">choose out their words.</hi> Note, An air of purity and piety in common conversation is a very happy omen to any people; other graces, other blessings, shall be given where God gives a pure language to those who have been a <hi type="italic">people of unclean lips.</hi> <div eID="gen20696" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20697" type="x-p"/> 2. That the worship of God, according to his will, shall be more closely applied to, and more unanimously concurred in. Instead of sacrifice and incense, they shall <hi type="italic">call upon the name of the Lord.</hi> Prayer is the spiritual offering with which God must be honoured; and, to prepare and fit us for that duty, it is necessary that we have a <hi type="italic">pure language.</hi> We are utterly unfit to take God's name into our lips, unless they be pure lips. The purifying of the language in common conversation is necessary to the acceptableness of the words of our mouth and the meditation of our heart on our devotion; for how can <hi type="italic">sweet waters and bitter</hi> come <hi type="italic">out of the same fountain?</hi> <reference osisRef="Jas.3.9-Jas.3.12">James iii. 9-12</reference>. It is likewise promised that their language being thus purified they shall serve God <hi type="italic">with one consent,</hi> with <hi type="italic">one shoulder</hi> (so the word is), alluding to oxen in the yoke, that draw even. When Christians are unanimous in the service of God the work goes on cheerfully. This is the effect of the pure language, purified from passion, envy, and censoriousness. Note, Purity is the way to unity; the reformation of manners is the way to a comprehension. <hi type="italic">The wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable.</hi> <div eID="gen20697" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20698" type="x-p"/> 3. That those that were driven from God shall return to him and be accepted of him (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.10">v. 10</reference>): <hi type="italic">From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,</hi> that is, from Egypt (so described, <reference osisRef="Isa.18.1">Isa. xviii. 1</reference>) or from some other very remote country—<hi type="italic">my suppliants, even the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring my offering.</hi> Those that by reason of their distance had almost forgotten God, their obligations to him, shall be put in mind of him, as the prodigal son was of his father's house, in the far country. Those that by reason of their dispersion, under the tokens of his displeasure, might be afraid of coming to him, yet even they shall be gathered under his wings; the <hi type="italic">daughter of his dispersed,</hi> that is <hi type="italic">afar off,</hi> will be found among those whom <hi type="italic">the Lord our God shall call;</hi> and, though they are dispersed, he will own them for his; his calling them <hi type="italic">my dispersed</hi> puts honour upon them, sufficient to counterbalance all the disgrace of their dispersion. These shall come, (1.) With their humble petitions: They are <hi type="italic">my suppliants.</hi> Note, True converts are suppliants to God; they do not plead, but <hi type="italic">make supplication to their Judge</hi> (<reference osisRef="Job.9.15">Job ix. 15</reference>); and wherever they are, though <hi type="italic">beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,</hi> a great way off from his house of prayer, he has his eye upon them and his ear open to them; they are his suppliants. (2.) With their spiritual sacrifices: <hi type="italic">They shall bring my offering,</hi> shall bring themselves as spiritual sacrifices to God (<reference osisRef="Rom.12.1">Rom. xii. 1</reference>); the conversion of the Gentiles is called <hi type="italic">the offering up of the Gentiles</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rom.15.16">Rom. xv. 16</reference>); and with themselves they shall bring the gospel-sacrifices of prayer, and praise, and alms, with which God is well pleased. <div eID="gen20698" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20699" type="x-p"/> 4. That sin and sinners shall be purged out from among them, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.11">v. 11</reference>. God will take away, (1.) Their just reproach: <hi type="italic">In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings.</hi> They shall be ashamed as penitents, and shall continue to be so (see <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.63">Ezek. xvi. 63</reference>), but they shall not be ashamed as sinners that return to folly again. "<hi type="italic">Thou shalt not be ashamed,</hi> that is, thou shalt no more do a shameful thing, as thou hast done." The guilt of sin being taken away by pardoning mercy, the reproach of it shall be rolled away from the sinner's own conscience, that being <hi type="italic">purified,</hi> and <hi type="italic">pacified,</hi> and <hi type="italic">cleansed from dead works.</hi> When wickedness and wicked people abound in a nation those few in it that are good are ashamed of them and of their land; but when sinners are converted, and the land reformed, that shame and the cause of it are removed. (2.) Their unjust glorying: "<hi type="italic">I will take away out of the midst of thee,</hi> not only the profane, who are a shame to thy land, but the hypocrites, who appear beautiful outwardly, and <hi type="italic">rejoice in thy pride,</hi> in the holy city, the holy house." These were indeed Israel's glory, but they made them their pride, and rejoiced in them, as if they were an invincible bulwark to secure them in their sinful ways; they relied on them as their righteousness and strength, boasting of <hi type="italic">the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord</hi> (<reference osisRef="Jer.7.4">Jer. vii. 4</reference>); they were <hi type="italic">haughty because of the holy mountain,</hi> were conceited of themselves, scornful of others, and set even the judgments of God at defiance. Note, Church-privileges, when they are not duly improved as they ought to be, are often made the matter of men's pride and the ground of their security. But that haughtiness is the most offensive to God which is supported and fed by the pretensions of holiness. This God will silence and take away. <div eID="gen20699" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20700" type="x-p"/> 5. That God will have a remnant of holy, humble, serious people among them, that shall have the comfort of their relation to him and interest in him (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.12">v. 12</reference>): <hi type="italic">I will leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people.</hi> When the Chaldeans carried away the Jews into captivity they <hi type="italic">left of the poor of the land for vine-dressers and husbandmen,</hi> a type and figure of God's distinguished remnant, whom he sets apart for himself. They are <hi type="italic">afflicted</hi> and <hi type="italic">poor,</hi> low in the world; such <hi type="italic">God has chosen,</hi> <reference osisRef="Jas.2.5">James ii. 5</reference>. The poor are evangelized, low in their own eyes, afflicted for sin, poor in spirit. They are God's leaving, for it is a <hi type="italic">remnant according to the election of grace. I have reserved them to myself,</hi> says God (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.4-Rom.11.5">Rom. xi. 4, 5</reference>), <hi type="italic">and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.</hi> Note, Those whom God designs for the glory of his name he enables to trust in his name; and the greater their affliction and poverty in the world are the more reason they see to trust in God, having nothing else to trust to, <reference osisRef="1Tim.5.5">1 Tim. v. 5</reference>. <div eID="gen20700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20701" type="x-p"/> 6. That this select remnant shall be blessed with purity and peace, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.13">v. 13</reference>. (1.) They shall be blessed with purity, both in words and actions: They <hi type="italic">shall neither do iniquity nor speak lies.</hi> Justice and veracity shall command them and govern them, though they be ever so much against their secular interest. They shall not only not speak a direct deliberate lie, but <hi type="italic">there shall not be a deceitful tongue found in their mouth,</hi> not in the mouth of any of them; not the least equivocation shall come from them. (2.) They shall be blessed with peace. They shall, as the sheep of God's pasture, <hi type="italic">feed</hi> and <hi type="italic">lie down, and none shall make them afraid.</hi> They shall not be fearful themselves, nor shall any about them be frightful to them. Note, Those that are careful not to do iniquity need not be afraid of any calamity, for it cannot hurt them, and therefore should not terrify them.
entries.5ec97e81450e0bfb5ad9cfd191cfac048985ac8f: <div eID="gen20701" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Evangelical Predictions. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 612.)</title> <div sID="gen20702" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">14</hi> Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. <hi type="super">15</hi> The <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more. <hi type="super">16</hi> In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem, Fear thou not: <hi type="italic">and to</hi> Zion, Let not thine hands be slack. <hi type="super">17</hi> The <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> thy God in the midst of thee <hi type="italic">is</hi> mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing. <hi type="super">18</hi> I will gather <hi type="italic">them that are</hi> sorrowful for the solemn assembly, <hi type="italic">who</hi> are of thee, <hi type="italic">to whom</hi> the reproach of it <hi type="italic">was</hi> a burden. <hi type="super">19</hi> Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee: and I will save her that halteth, and gather her that was driven out; and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame. <hi type="super">20</hi> At that time will I bring you <hi type="italic">again,</hi> even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <div eID="gen20702" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20703" type="x-p"/> After the promises of the taking away of sin, here follow promises of the taking away of trouble; for when the cause is removed the effect will cease. What makes a people holy will make them happy of course. The precious promises here made to the purified people were to have their full accomplishment in the comforts of the gospel, in the hope, and much more in the enjoyment, of which, they are here called upon, 1. To rejoice and sing (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.14">v. 14</reference>): <hi type="italic">Sing, O daughter of Zion!</hi> sing for joy; <hi type="italic">Shout, O Israel!</hi> in a holy transport and exultation; <hi type="italic">be glad and rejoice with all the heart;</hi> let the joy be inward, let it be great. Those that love God with all their heart have occasion with all their heart to rejoice in him. It was promised (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.13">v. 13</reference>) that their sins should be mortified and their fears silenced, and then follows, <hi type="italic">Sing</hi> and <hi type="italic">rejoice.</hi> Note, Those that reform have cause to rejoice, whereas Israel cannot rejoice for joy as other people, while she goes a whoring from her God. God's promises, applied by faith, furnish the saints with constant and abundant matter for joy; they are filled with joy and peace in believing them. 2. To throw off all their discouragements (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.16">v. 16</reference>): <hi type="italic">In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem</hi> (God will say it by his prophets, by his providences, their neighbours shall say it, they shall say it to one another), "<hi type="italic">Fear thou not,</hi> be not disposed to fear, do not easily admit the impressions of it; when things are bad, fear not their being worse, but hope they will mend; frighten not thyself upon every occasion. <hi type="italic">Let not thy hands be slack</hi> or <hi type="italic">faint;</hi> wring not thy hands in despair; drop not thy hands in despondence; disfit not thyself for thy work and warfare by giving way to doubts and fears. Pluck up thy spirits, and, in token of that, lift up thy hands, the <hi type="italic">hands that hung down,</hi> <reference osisRef="Heb.12.12">Heb. xii. 12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.35.3">Isa. xxxv. 3</reference>. Lift up thy hands in prayer to God; lift up thy hands to help thyself." Fear makes the hands slack, but faith and hope make them vigorous, and the joy of the Lord will be our strength both for doing and suffering. <div eID="gen20703" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20704" type="x-p"/> Let us now see what these precious promises are which are here made to the people of God, for the banishing of their griefs and fears and the encouraging of their hopes and joys; and to us are these promises made as well as to them. <div eID="gen20704" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20705" type="x-p"/> I. An end shall be put to all their troubles and distresses (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.15">v. 15</reference>): "<hi type="italic">The Lord has taken away thy judgments,</hi> has removed all the calamities thou hast been groaning under, which were the punishments of thy sin; the noise of war shall be silenced, the reproach of famine done away, and the captivity brought back. Though some grievances remain, they shall be only afflictions, and not judgments, for sin shall be pardoned. <hi type="italic">He has cast out thy enemy,</hi> that has thrust himself into thy land, and triumphed over thee. He has <hi type="italic">swept out thy enemy</hi>" (so some read it), "as dirt is swept out of the house to the dunghill." When they sweep out their sins with the besom of reformation God will sweep out their enemies with the besom of destruction. If they should need correction, they shall fall into the hands of the Lord, whose mercies are great, and shall not again fall into the hands of man, whose tender mercies are cruel: "<hi type="italic">Thou shalt not see evil any more,</hi> not such evil days as thou hast seen." Note, The way to get clear of the evil of trouble is to keep clear from the evil of sin; and to those that do so trouble has no real evil in it. <div eID="gen20705" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20706" type="x-p"/> II. God will give them the tokens of his presence with them; though he has long seemed to stand at a distance (they having provoked him to withdraw), he will make it to appear that he is <hi type="italic">with them of a truth: "The Lord is in the midst of thee, O Zion!</hi> of thee, <hi type="italic">O Jerusalem!</hi> as the sun in the centre of the universe, to diffuse his light and influence upon every part. He is <hi type="italic">in the midst of thee,</hi> to preside in all thy affairs and to take care of all thy interests." And, 1. "He is the <hi type="italic">King of Israel</hi> (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.15">v. 15</reference>) and is in the midst of thee as a king in the midst of his people." With an eye to this, our Lord Jesus is called the <hi type="italic">King of Israel</hi> (<reference osisRef="John.1.49">John i. 49</reference>); and he is, and will be, in the midst of his church always, even to the end of the world, to receive the homage of his subjects, and to give out his favours to them, even <hi type="italic">where</hi> but <hi type="italic">two or three are gathered together in his name.</hi> 2. "He is the Lord thy God, thine in covenant, and he is in the midst of thee as thy God, whom thou hast an interest in and whose own thou art. He has put himself into dear relations to thee, laid himself by promise under obligations to thee, and, that thou mayest have abundant comfort in both, he <hi type="italic">is in the midst of thee,</hi> nigh at hand to answer both." 3. "He that is in the midst of thee as thy God and King is <hi type="italic">mighty,</hi> is almighty, is able to do all that for thee that thou needest and canst desire." 4. "He has engaged his power for thy succour: <hi type="italic">He will save. He will be Jesus,</hi> will answer the name, for he will save his people from their sins." <div eID="gen20706" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20707" type="x-p"/> III. God will take delight in them, and in doing them good. The expressions of this are very lively and affecting (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.17">v. 17</reference>): <hi type="italic">He will rejoice over thee with joy,</hi> will not only be well pleased with thee, upon thy repentance and reformation, and take thee into favour, but will take a complacency in thee, as the bridegroom does in his bride, or the bride in her ornaments, <reference osisRef="Isa.62.3-Isa.62.5">Isa. lxii. 3-5</reference>. The conversion of sinners and the consolation of saints are the joy of angels, for they are the joy of God him-self. The church should be the <hi type="italic">joy of the whole earth</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.48.2">Ps. xlviii. 2</reference>), for it is the joy of the whole heaven. He will <hi type="italic">rest in his love,</hi> will be <hi type="italic">silent in his love,</hi> so the word is. "I will not rebuke thee as I have done, for thy sins; I will acquiesce in thee, and in my relation to thee." I know not where there is the like expression of Christ's love to his church, unless in that song of songs, <reference osisRef="Song.4.9">Cant. iv. 9</reference>, <hi type="italic">Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse, with one of thy eyes.</hi> O the condescensions of divine grace! The great God not only loves his saints, but he loves to love them, is pleased that he has pitched upon these objects of his love. He <hi type="italic">will joy over them with singing.</hi> He that is grieved for the sin of sinners rejoices in the graces and services of the saints, and is ready to express that joy by singing over them. <hi type="italic">The Lord takes plea-sure in those that fear him,</hi> and in them Jesus Christ will shortly be glorified and admired. <div eID="gen20707" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20708" type="x-p"/> IV. God will comfort Zion's mourners, who sympathize with her in her griefs, and will wipe away their tears (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.18">v. 18</reference>): <hi type="italic">I will gather those who are sorrowful for the solemn assemblies, to whom the reproach of it was a burden.</hi> See, 1. Who those are whom God will rejoice in and make to rejoice. They are such as are sorrowful. Those only must expect to reap in joy that sow in tears. The sorrowful now shall be for ever joyful. 2. What is the great matter of sorrow to Zion's mourners, when Zion is in mourning. Many are her calamities. The city is ruined, and the palaces are demolished; trade is at an end, and the administration of public justice; but all these are nothing to them in comparison with the desolations of the sanctuary, the destruction of the temple and the altar, to attend on which, in solemn feasts, all Israel used to come together three times a year. It is for those sacred solemn assemblies that they are sorrowful, (1.) Because they are dispersed; there is no temple to come up to, or, if there were, no people to come up to it; so that the <hi type="italic">solemn feasts and sabbaths are forgotten in Zion,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lam.2.6">Lam. ii. 6</reference>. Note, The restraining of public assemblies for religious worship, the scattering of them by their enemies, or the forsaking of them by their friends, so that either there are no assemblies or not solemn ones, is a very sorrowful thing to all good people. If <hi type="italic">the ways of Zion mourn,</hi> the sons of Zion mourn too. And hereby they make it to appear that they are indeed of Zion, living members of that body with the grievances of which they are so sensibly affected. (2.) Because they are despised; the reproach of the solemn assemblies is a burden to them. It had been the lot of the solemn assemblies to lie under a great deal of reproach. Satan and his instruments having a particular spite at them, as the great support of the interest of God's kingdom among men. Black and odious characters have been put upon those assemblies; and this is a burden to all those that have a cordial concern for the glory of God and the welfare of the souls of men. They reckon that the reproaches of those who reproach the solemn assemblies fall upon them, fall foul upon them. <div eID="gen20708" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20709" type="x-p"/> V. God will recover the captives out of the hands of their oppressors, and bring home the banished that seemed to be expelled, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.19-Zeph.3.20">v. 19, 20</reference>. 1. Their enemies shall be disabled to detain them in bondage: "<hi type="italic">At that time I will undo all that afflict thee,</hi> will break their power, and blast their counsels, so that they shall be forced to surrender the prey they have taken." <hi type="italic">Conficiam—I will take them to task;</hi> "I will be doing with them shortly, and so as to make an end of them." Note, Those that abuse and oppress God's people take the ready way to undo themselves. 2. They shall be enabled to assert and recover their liberty, and all the difficulties in the way of it shall be surmounted. Is the church weak and wounded? <hi type="italic">I will save her that halts,</hi> as was promised, <reference osisRef="Mic.4.7">Mic. iv. 7</reference>. He will help her when she cannot help herself; even <hi type="italic">the lame shall take the prey,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.33.23">Isa. xxxiii. 23</reference>. Is she dispersed, and not likely to incorporate for her common benefit? I will <hi type="italic">gather her that was driven out,</hi> and <hi type="italic">bring her again at the time that I gather her.</hi> One act of mercy and grace shall serve both to collect them out of their dispersions and to conduct them to their own land. When the <hi type="italic">people's hearts are prepared,</hi> the work will be done suddenly; and who can hinder it if God undertake to effect it? "<hi type="italic">I will turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord;</hi> you shall plainly discern the hand of God in it, and say, <hi type="italic">This is the Lord's doing.</hi>" <div eID="gen20709" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20710" type="x-p"/> VI. God will by all this put honour upon them and gain them respect from all about them. Israel was at first <hi type="italic">made high above all nations in praise and fame,</hi> <reference osisRef="Deut.26.19">Deut. xxvi. 19</reference>. The reproach brought upon them was therefore one of the sorest of their grievances (nothing cuts deeper to those that are in honour than disgrace does); and therefore when God returns, in mercy, to his church, it is here promised that she shall regain her credit; all the reproach shall be for ever rolled way, as Israel's at Gilgal, <reference osisRef="Josh.5.9">Josh. v. 9</reference>. The church shall be as honourable as ever she had been despicable. 1. Even those that reproached her shall be made to respect her: "<hi type="italic">I will get them praise and fame in every land, where they have been put to shame,</hi> that the same who were the witnesses of their disgrace may see cause to change their mind concerning them." Those that said, "This is Zion whom no man looks after," shall say, "This is Zion whom the great God looks after." And she that was looked upon to be the <hi type="italic">offscouring of the earth</hi> now appears to be the darling of heaven. 2. Even those that never knew her shall be brought to honour her (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.20">v. 20</reference>): <hi type="italic">I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth.</hi> So the Jewish church was when <hi type="italic">the fear of the Jews</hi> fell upon their neighbours (<reference osisRef="Esth.8.17">Esth. viii. 17</reference>), and some of all nations said, <hi type="italic">we will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you,</hi> <reference osisRef="Zech.8.23">Zech. viii. 23</reference>. So the Christian church was when it was made to flourish in the world, for there is that in it which may justly recommend it to the value and esteem of all the people of the earth. And so the universal church of the firstborn will be in the great day, when the saints shall be brought together to Christ, that he may be admired and glorified in them, and they admired and glorified in him before angels and men. Then will God's Israel be <hi type="italic">made a name and a praise</hi> to eternity.  <chapter eID="Zeph.3"/> <div eID="gen20710" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen20642" osisID="Zeph" type="book"/>

entries.62a51c8935a5e0e788d6eb3a446a6deb74abf0be: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12955"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 3</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Zeph.3.1-Zeph.3.20">Zep 3:1-20</reference>. Resumption of the Denunciation of Jerusalem, as Being Unreformed by the Punishment of Other Nations: After Her Chastisement Jehovah Will Interpose for Her against Her Foes; His Worship Shall Flourish in All Lands, Beginning at Jerusalem, Where He Shall Be in the Midst of His People, and Shall Make Them a Praise in All the Earth.</title> <div sID="gen24265" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12955"/><hi type="bold">1. filthy--</hi>Maurer translates from a different root, "rebellious," "contumacious." But the following term, "polluted," refers rather to her inward moral filth, in spite of her outward ceremonial purity [Calvin]. Grotius says, the Hebrew is used of women who have prostituted their virtue. There is in the Hebrew Moreah; a play on the name Moriah, the hill on which the temple was built; implying the glaring contrast between their filthiness and the holiness of the worship on Moriah in which they professed to have a share.<div eID="gen24265" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24266" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">oppressing--</hi>namely, the poor, weak, widows, orphans and strangers (<reference osisRef="Jer.22.3">Jr 22:3</reference>). <div eID="gen24266" type="x-p"/>
entries.9a6dead32fdfde1ccf436e56799eced31450de56: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12956"/><div sID="gen24267" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12956"/><hi type="bold">2. received not correction--</hi>Jerusalem is incurable, obstinately rejecting salutary admonition, and refusing to be reformed by "correction" (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.3">Jr 5:3</reference>).<div eID="gen24267" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24268" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">trusted not in ... Lord--</hi>Distrust in the Lord as if He were insufficient, is the parent of all superstitions and wickednesses [Calvin].<div eID="gen24268" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24269" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">drew not near to her God--</hi>Though God was specially near to her (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.7">De 4:7</reference>) as "her God," yet she drew not near to Him, but gratuitously estranged herself from Him. <div eID="gen24269" type="x-p"/>
entries.a39c070aaf015776f379354fdcc90034af9a255b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12957"/><div sID="gen24270" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12957"/><hi type="bold">3. roaring--</hi>for prey (<reference osisRef="Prov.28.15">Pr 28:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.22.27">Eze 22:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.3.4">Am 3:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.2.2">Mi 2:2</reference>).<div eID="gen24270" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24271" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">evening wolves--</hi>which are most ravenous at evening after being foodless all day (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.6">Jr 5:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hab.1.8">Ha 1:8</reference>).<div eID="gen24271" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24272" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they gnaw not the bones till the morrow--</hi>rather, "they put not off till to-morrow to gnaw the bones"; but devour all at once, bones and flesh, so ragingly ravenous are they [Calvin]. <div eID="gen24272" type="x-p"/>
entries.2761e3911742fad561ad48cde97e5fc1a32ea82c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12958"/><div sID="gen24273" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12958"/><hi type="bold">4. light--</hi>in whose life and teaching there is no truth, gravity, or steadiness.<div eID="gen24273" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24274" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">treacherous--</hi>false to Jehovah, whose prophets they profess to be (<reference osisRef="Jer.23.32">Jr 23:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.22.28">Eze 22:28</reference>).<div eID="gen24274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24275" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">polluted ... sanctuary--</hi>by their profane deeds. <div eID="gen24275" type="x-p"/>
entries.94b482ab1f667e3440467366bd61c184f730af82: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12959"/><div sID="gen24276" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12959"/>5-7. The Jews regard not God's justice manifested in the midst of them, nor His judgments on the guilty nations around.<div eID="gen24276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24277" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">The just Lord--</hi>Why then are ye so unjust?<div eID="gen24277" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24278" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">is in the midst thereof--</hi>He retorts on them their own boast, "Is not the Lord among us" (<reference osisRef="Mic.3.11">Mi 3:11</reference>)? True He is, but it is for another end from what ye think [Calvin]; namely, to lead you by the example of His righteousness to be righteous. <reference osisRef="Lev.19.2">Le 19:2</reference>, "Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy" [Maurer]. But Calvin, "That ye may feel His hand to be the nearer for taking vengeance for your crimes: 'He will not do iniquity' by suffering your sins to go unpunished" (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.4">De 32:4</reference>).<div eID="gen24278" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24279" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">every morning--</hi>literally, "morning by morning." The time in the sultry East for dispensing justice.<div eID="gen24279" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24280" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bring ... to light--</hi>publicly and manifestly by the teaching of His prophets, which aggravates their guilt; also by samples of His judgments on the guilty.<div eID="gen24280" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24281" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he faileth not--</hi>He is continually setting before you samples of His justice, sparing no pains. Compare <reference osisRef="Isa.5.4">Is 5:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.50.4">50:4</reference>, "he wakeneth morning by morning."<div eID="gen24281" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24282" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">knoweth no shame--</hi>The unjust Jews are not shamed by His justice into repentance. <div eID="gen24282" type="x-p"/>
entries.b4e18212e965a649c74a4bb55ea975ebb0f3b6b7: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12962"/><div sID="gen24290" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12962"/><hi type="bold">8. wait ye upon me--</hi>Here Jehovah turns to the pious Jews. Amidst all these judgments on the Jewish nation, look forward to the glorious time of restoration to be ushered in by God's precious outpouring of wrath on all nations, <reference osisRef="Isa.30.18-Isa.30.33">Is 30:18-33</reference>; where the same phrase, "blessed are all they that wait for Him," is used as to the same great event. Calvin erroneously makes this verse an address to the ungodly; and so Maurer, "Ye shall not have to wait for Me in vain"; I will presently come armed with indignation: I will no longer contend with you by My prophets.<div eID="gen24290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24291" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">until the day--</hi>that is, waiting for the day (<reference osisRef="Hab.2.3">Ha 2:3</reference>).<div eID="gen24291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24292" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rise up to the prey--</hi>like a savage beast rising from his lair, greedy for the prey (compare <reference osisRef="Matt.24.28">Mt 24:28</reference>). Or rather, as a warrior leading Israel to certain victory, which is expressed by "the prey," or booty, which is the reward of victory. The Septuagint and Syriac versions read the Hebrew, "I rise up as a witness" (compare <reference osisRef="Job.16.8">Job 16:8</reference>; Mal 3:5). Jehovah being in this view witness, accuser, and judge. English Version is better (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.33.23">Is 33:23</reference>).<div eID="gen24292" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24293" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">gather the nations--</hi>against Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Zech.14.2">Zec 14:2</reference>), to pour out His indignation upon them there (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">Joe 3:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.2">Zec 12:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.12.3">3</reference>). <div eID="gen24293" type="x-p"/>
entries.fc9745e252544ffc7c3c6e9b4a852579df54133c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12963"/><div sID="gen24294" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12963"/><hi type="bold">9. For--</hi>The blessed things promised in this and <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.10">Zep 3:10</reference> are the immediate results of the punishment inflicted on the nations, mentioned in <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.8">Zep 3:8</reference> (compare <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.19">Zep 3:19</reference>).<div eID="gen24294" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24295" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">turn to the people a pure language--</hi>that is, changing their impure language I will give to them again a pure language (literally, "lip"). Compare for this Hebrew idiom, <reference osisRef="1Sam.10.9">1Sa 10:9</reference>, Margin. The confusion of languages was of the penalty sin, probably idolatry at Babel (<reference osisRef="Gen.11.1-Gen.11.6">Ge 11:1-6</reference>, Margin, where also "lip" expresses language, and perhaps also religion; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.4">Zep 3:4</reference>, "a tower whose top may reach unto heaven," or rather, points to heaven, namely, dedicated to the heavens idolized, or Bel); certainly, of rebellion against God's will. An earnest of the removal of this penalty was the gift of tongues on Pentecost (<reference osisRef="Acts.2.6-Acts.2.13">Ac 2:6-13</reference>). The full restoration of the earth's unity of language and of worship is yet future, and is connected with the restoration of the Jews, to be followed by the conversion of the world. Compare <reference osisRef="Isa.19.18">Is 19:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.9">Zec 14:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.15.6">Ro 15:6</reference>, "with one mind and one mouth glorify God." The Gentiles' lips have been rendered impure through being the instruments of calling on idols and dishonoring God (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.16.4">Psa 16:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.17">Ho 2:17</reference>). Whether Hebrew shall be the one universal language or not, the God of the Hebrews shall be the one only object of worship. Until the Holy Ghost purify the lips, we cannot rightly call upon God (<reference osisRef="Isa.6.5-Isa.6.7">Is 6:5-7</reference>).<div eID="gen24295" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24296" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">serve him with one consent--</hi>literally, "shoulder" or "back"; metaphor from a yoke, or burden, borne between two (<reference osisRef="Num.13.23">Nu 13:23</reference>); helping one another with conjoint effort. If one of the two bearers of a burden, laid on both conjointly, give way, the burden must fall to the earth [Calvin]. Christ's rule is called a burden (<reference osisRef="Matt.11.30">Mt 11:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.15.28">Ac 15:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.24">Re 2:24</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="2Cor.6.14">2Co 6:14</reference> for the same image). <div eID="gen24296" type="x-p"/>
entries.dd3eb476c287113b67fb3267acb52751496ffe64: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12964"/><div sID="gen24297" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12964"/><hi type="bold">10. From beyond ... Ethiopia my suppliants--</hi>literally, "burners of incense" (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.141.2">Psa 141:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.5.8">Re 5:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.8.3">8:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.8.4">4</reference>). The Israelites are meant, called "the daughter of My dispersed," a Hebrew idiom for My dispersed people. "The rivers of Ethiopia" are those which enclose it on the north. In the west of Abyssinia there has long existed a people called Falashas, or "emigrants" (akin to the synonym "Philistine"). These trace their origin to Palestine and profess the Jewish religion. In physical traits they resemble the Arabs. When Bruce was there, they had a Jewish king, Gideon, and his queen, Judith. Probably the Abyssinian Christians were originally in part converted Jews. They are here made the representatives of all Israel which is to be restored.<div eID="gen24297" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24298" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall bring mine offering--</hi>that is, the offering that is My right. I prefer, with De Wette and Chaldee Version, making "suppliants" the objective case, not the nominative. The peoples: (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.8">Zep 3:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.9">9</reference>), brought to fear Me by My judgments, "shall bring as Mine offering My suppliants (an appropriate term for the Jews, on whom then there shall have been poured the spirit of supplications, <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">Zec 12:10</reference>), the daughter of My dispersed." So <reference osisRef="Isa.66.20">Is 66:20</reference>, "they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord." Compare Horsley's view of <reference osisRef="Isa.18.1">Is 18:1</reference>, 2, 7. England in this view may be the naval power to restore Israel to Palestine (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.9">Is 60:9</reference>). The Hebrew for "Ethiopia" is Cush, which may include not only Ethiopia, but also the region of the Tigris and Babylon, where Nimrod, Cush's son (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.8-Gen.10.12">Ge 10:8-12</reference>), founded Nineveh and acquired Babylon, and where the ten tribes are mentioned as being scattered (<reference osisRef="1Pet.1.1">1Pe 1:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.5.13">5:13</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Isa.11.11">Is 11:11</reference>). The restoration under Cyrus of the Jews transported under Pharaoh-necho to Egypt and Ethiopia, was an earnest of the future restoration under Christ. <div eID="gen24298" type="x-p"/>
entries.ab5c808c28816dac81843855e017e0c72ede02d5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12965"/><div sID="gen24299" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12965"/><hi type="bold">11. shalt thou not be ashamed--</hi>Thou shalt then have no cause to be ashamed; for I will then take away out of the midst of thee those who by their sins gave thee cause for shame (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.7">Zep 3:7</reference>).<div eID="gen24299" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24300" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">them that rejoice in thy pride--</hi>those priding themselves on that which thou boastest of, thy temple ("My holy mountain"), thy election as God's people, &c., in the Pharisaic spirit (<reference osisRef="Jer.7.4">Jr 7:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.3.11">Mi 3:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.3.9">Mt 3:9</reference>). Compare <reference osisRef="Jer.13.17">Jr 13:17</reference>, "mine eyes shall weep for your pride." The converted remnant shall be of a humble spirit (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.12">Zep 3:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.66.2">Is 66:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.66.10">10</reference>). <div eID="gen24300" type="x-p"/>
entries.0075be79f9a210705af192dd5cd9cc1c277e5d99: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12966"/><div sID="gen24301" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12966"/><hi type="bold">12. afflicted ... they shall trust in ... Lord--</hi>the blessed effect of sanctified affliction on the Jewish remnant. Entire trust in the Lord cannot be, except where all cause for boasting is taken away (<reference osisRef="Isa.14.32">Is 14:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.11.11">Zec 11:11</reference>). <div eID="gen24301" type="x-p"/>
entries.2792641e6ce11cbf7b19aad562b89c3745b5a65c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12967"/><div sID="gen24302" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12967"/><hi type="bold">13. nor speak lies--</hi>worshipping God in truth, and towards man having love without dissimulation. The characteristic of the 144,000 sealed of Israel.<div eID="gen24302" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24303" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">none shall make them afraid--</hi>either foreign foe, or unjust prince (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.3">Zep 3:3</reference>), prophet, or priest (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.4">Zep 3:4</reference>). <div eID="gen24303" type="x-p"/>
entries.c566d83663a330b7c2855bf8c1d6ad71953c1bdf: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12968"/><div sID="gen24304" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12968"/>14. The prophet in mental vision sees the joyful day of Zion present, and bids her rejoice at it. <div eID="gen24304" type="x-p"/>
entries.4b0a2d675102dcb1778a5a6f0b640ec50764a9ab: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12969"/><div sID="gen24305" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12969"/>15. The cause for joy: "The Lord hath taken away thy judgments," namely, those sent by Him upon thee. After the taking away of sin (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.13">Zep 3:13</reference>) follows the taking away of trouble. When the cause is removed, the effect will cease. Happiness follows in the wake of holiness.<div eID="gen24305" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24306" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the Lord is in the midst of thee--</hi>Though He seemed to desert thee for a time, He is now present as thy safeguard (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.17">Zep 3:17</reference>).<div eID="gen24306" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24307" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not see evil any more--</hi>Thou shalt not experience it (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.12">Jr 5:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.44.17">44:17</reference>). <div eID="gen24307" type="x-p"/>
entries.0f6e729997e0cb6b053f16a6e053c3b5a6763f0f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12970"/><div sID="gen24308" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12970"/><hi type="bold">16. Let not thine hands be slack--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Heb.12.12">He 12:12</reference>). Do not faint in the work of the Lord. <div eID="gen24308" type="x-p"/>
entries.2035058adbb4ef5812d7ad706d67867603b85700: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12971"/><div sID="gen24309" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12971"/><hi type="bold">17. he will rest in his love--</hi>content with it as His supreme delight (compare <reference osisRef="Luke.15.7">Lu 15:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.15.10">10</reference>) [Calvin], (<reference osisRef="Isa.62.5">Is 62:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.65.19">65:19</reference>). Or, He shall be silent, namely as to thy faults, not imputing them to thee [Maurer] (<reference osisRef="Ps.32.2">Psa 32:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.33.16">Eze 33:16</reference>). I prefer explaining it of that calm silent joy in the possession of the object of one's love, too great for words to express: just as God after the six days of creation rested with silent satisfaction in His work, for "behold it was very good" (<reference osisRef="Gen.1.31">Ge 1:31</reference>; 2:2). So the parallel clause by contrast expresses the joy, not kept silent as this, but uttered in "singing." <div eID="gen24309" type="x-p"/>
entries.3929969a5a165ad7fd2f4590cfcd7e10902412f6: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12972"/><div sID="gen24310" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12972"/><hi type="bold">18. sorrowful for the solemn assembly--</hi>pining after the solemn assembly which they cannot celebrate in exile (<reference osisRef="Lam.1.4">La 1:4</reference>; 2:6).<div eID="gen24310" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24311" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">who are of thee--</hi>that is, of thy true citizens; and whom therefore I will restore.<div eID="gen24311" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24312" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to whom the reproach of it was a burden--</hi>that is, to whom thy reproach ("the reproach of My people," <reference osisRef="Mic.6.16">Mi 6:16</reference>; their ignominious captivity) was a burden. "Of it" is put of thee, as the person is often changed. Those who shared in the burden of reproach which fell on My people. Compare <reference osisRef="Isa.25.8">Is 25:8</reference>, "the rebuke of His people shall He take away from off all the earth." <div eID="gen24312" type="x-p"/>
entries.24eaa8b1ae32df3526101edd32f96f5c02393b30: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12973"/><div sID="gen24313" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12973"/><hi type="bold">19. undo--</hi>Maurer translates, "I will deal with," that is, as they deserve. Compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.23.25">Eze 23:25</reference>, where the Hebrew is similarly translated. The destruction of Israel's foes precedes Israel's restoration (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.15">Is 66:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.66.16">16</reference>).<div eID="gen24313" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24314" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">her that halteth--</hi>all that are helpless. Their weakness will be no barrier in the way of My restoring them. So in <reference osisRef="Ps.35.15">Psa 35:15</reference>, Margin, "halting" is used for adversity. Also <reference osisRef="Ezek.34.16">Eze 34:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.4.6">Mi 4:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.4.7">7</reference>.<div eID="gen24314" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24315" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will get them praise, &c.--</hi>literally, "I will make them (to become) a praise and a name," &c.<div eID="gen24315" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24316" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shame--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ezek.34.29">Eze 34:29</reference>). <div eID="gen24316" type="x-p"/>
entries.185875b92fdf2b72426dab93eb5f05ee6e728b2c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12974"/><div sID="gen24317" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12974"/><hi type="bold">20. make you a name ... praise--</hi>make you to become celebrated and praised.<div eID="gen24317" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24318" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">turn back your captivity--</hi>bring back your captives [Maurer]. The Hebrew is plural, "captivities"; to express the captivities of different ages of their history, as well as the diversity of places in which they were and are dispersed.<div eID="gen24318" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24319" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">before your eyes--</hi>Incredible as the event may seem, your own eyes with delight shall see it. You will scarcely believe it for joy, but the testimony of your own eyes shall convince you of the delightful reality (compare <reference osisRef="Luke.24.41">Lu 24:41</reference>). <chapter eID="Zeph.3"/><div eID="gen24319" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen24166" osisID="Zeph" type="book"/>

entries.3a4c27d2f3360349e9a113a96bfc16fb6e7a867e: <div eID="gen35292" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen35293" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen35294" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen35294" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen35293" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen35295" type="x-p"/> The prophet reproves Jerusalem, and all her guides and rulers, for their obstinate perseverance in impiety, notwithstanding all the warnings and corrections which they had received from God, <reference osisRef="Zep.3.1-Zep.3.7">Zep 3:1-7</reference>. They are encouraged, however, after they shall have been chastised for their idolatry, and cured of it, to look for mercy and restoration, <reference osisRef="Zep.3.8-Zep.3.13">Zep 3:8-13</reference>; and exited to hymns of joy at the glorious prospect, <reference osisRef="Zep.3.14-Zep.3.17">Zep 3:14-17</reference>. After which the prophet concludes with large promises of favor and prosperity in the days of the Messiah, <reference osisRef="Zep.3.18-Zep.3.20">Zep 3:18-20</reference>. We take this extensive view of the concluding verses of this chapter, because an apostle has expressly assured us that in Every prophetical book of the Old Testament Scriptures are confined predictions relative to the Gospel dispensation. See <reference osisRef="Act.3.24">Act 3:24</reference>. <div eID="gen35295" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35296" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen35296" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35297" type="x-p"/> Wo to her that is filthy - This is a denunciation of Divine judgment against Jerusalem.
entries.823db7142b380846cb2b6bf7c4641de9321925bc: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen35297" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35298" type="x-p"/> She obeyed not the voice - Of conscience, of God, and of his prophets. <div eID="gen35298" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35299" type="x-p"/> She received not correction - Did not profit by his chastisements; was uneasy and ill-tempered under her afflictions, and derived no manner of good from these chastisements. <div eID="gen35299" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35300" type="x-p"/> She trusted not in the Lord - Did not consider him as the Fountain whence all help and salvation should come; and rather sought for support from man and herself, than from God. <div eID="gen35300" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35301" type="x-p"/> She drew not near to her God - Did not worship him; did not walk in his ways; did not make prayer and supplication to him.
entries.d0ac920264658d97140b83ca89361c8422c34de6: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen35301" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35302" type="x-p"/> Her princes - are roaring lions - Tearing all to pieces without shadow of law, except their own despotic power. <div eID="gen35302" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35303" type="x-p"/> Her judges are evening wolves - Being a little afraid of the lion-like princes, they practice their unjust dealings from evening to morning, and take the day to find their rest. <div eID="gen35303" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35304" type="x-p"/> They gnaw not the bones till the morrow - They devour the flesh in the night, and gnaw the bones and extract the marrow afterwards. They use all violence and predatory oppression, like wild beasts; they shun the light, and turn day into night by their revellings.
entries.055d36029f7441797f65ac0aa67776112d2538a6: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen35304" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35305" type="x-p"/> Her prophets are light and treacherous persons - They have no seriousness, no deep conviction of the awful nature of their office, no concern for the immortal souls of the people. Treacherous persons - they betray the souls of the people for the sake of worldly honor, pleasure, and profit. Even in our own enlightened country we find prophets who prefer hunting the hare or the fox, and pursuing the partridge and pheasant, to visiting the sick, and going after the strayed, lost sheep of the house of Israel. Poor souls! They know neither God nor themselves; and if they did visit the sick, they could not speak to them to exhortation, edification, or comfort. God never called them to his work; therefore they know nothing of it. But O, what an account have these pleasure-taking false prophets to render to the Shepherd of souls! <div eID="gen35305" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35306" type="x-p"/> They have done violence to the law - They have forced wrong constructions on it in order to excuse themselves, and lull the people into spiritual slumber. So we find that it was an ancient practice for men to wrest the Scriptures to their own destruction.
entries.81b2b5ec30b88a39d880aaa111c25e6b700b74e4: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen35306" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35307" type="x-p"/> The just Lord is in the midst thereof - He sees, marks down, and will punish all these wickednesses. <div eID="gen35307" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35308" type="x-p"/> Every morning doth he bring his judgment to light - The sense is, says Bp. Newcome, "Not a day passes but we see instances of his goodness to righteous men, and of his vengeance on the wicked."
entries.49441ca42065b59cd6e46e522fe1ede0ad58fee7: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen35308" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35309" type="x-p"/> I have cut off the nations - Syria, Israel, and those referred to, <reference osisRef="Isa.36.18">Isa 36:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.36.20">Isa 36:20</reference>. - Newcome.
entries.e5517749a71344336f086254786a0ce13aa8b1a6: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen35309" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35310" type="x-p"/> Surely thou wilt fear me - After so many displays of my sovereign power and judgments. <div eID="gen35310" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35311" type="x-p"/> But they rose early - And instead of returning to God, they practiced every abomination. They were diligent to find out times and places for their iniquity. This is the worst state of man.
entries.e7f87c998ea97c10c234f986e1cb04a7c36dfc86: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen35311" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35312" type="x-p"/> Wait ye upon me - Expect the fulfilment of all my promises and threatenings: I am God, and change not. <div eID="gen35312" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35313" type="x-p"/> For all the earth - All the land of Judah.
entries.fa8b9a7fcedf12aa448c32adc2db9ad0806ceb0e: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen35313" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35314" type="x-p"/> Will I turn to the people - This promise must refer to the conversion of the Jews under the Gospel. <div eID="gen35314" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35315" type="x-p"/> That they may all call - That the whole nation may invoke God by Christ, and serve him with one consent; not one unbeliever being found among them. <div eID="gen35315" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35316" type="x-p"/> The pure language, שפה ברורה saphah berurah, may here mean the form of religious worship. They had been before idolaters: now God promises to restore his pure worship among them. The word has certainly this meaning in <reference osisRef="Psa.81.6">Psa 81:6</reference>; where, as God is the speaker, the words should not be rendered, "I heard a language which I understood not," but, "I heard a religious confession, which I approved not." See <reference osisRef="Isa.19.18">Isa 19:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.14.3">Hos 14:3</reference>; and see <reference osisRef="Joe.2.28">Joe 2:28</reference>, where a similar promise is found.
entries.30b536c2afaaa2d02f7ba665b4b29967f1faf1ea: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen35316" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35317" type="x-p"/> From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia - This may denote both Africa and the southern Arabia. Bochart thinks that Arabia Chusaer is meant; and that the rivers are Besor, which flows into the Mediterranean; Rhinocorura, which flows into the Lake Sirbonis; Trajanus Amnis, which flows into the Red Sea; and the river Corys. Calmet thinks that these rivers mean the Nile, which by seven mouths falls into the Mediterranean. The Nile comes from Ethiopia, properly so called; and runs through all Egypt, and falls into the sea at that part of Arabia which the Scripture calls Cush or Ethiopia. <div eID="gen35317" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35318" type="x-p"/> My dispersed - The Jews, scattered through different parts of the world. Shall bring mine offering. Shall acknowledge my mercy in sending them the Messiah to bless them, by turning every one of them away from their iniquities.
entries.e6a58a807a5ab424758d36c926d7043500b19219: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen35318" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35319" type="x-p"/> Shalt thou not be ashamed - Thy punishment shall cease, for God shall pardon thy sin. <div eID="gen35319" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35320" type="x-p"/> For then I will take away out of the midst of thee - The wicked Jewish priests and scribes who blasphemed Christ, and would not come under his yoke. <div eID="gen35320" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35321" type="x-p"/> Because of my holy mountain - Thou wilt no more boast in my temple, but become meek and lowly in following him who is meek and lowly in heart, that ye may obtain rest to your souls.
entries.e1c05ca9676143c95aee14f9e078d30d7fd5a4ed: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen35321" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35322" type="x-p"/> An afflicted and poor people - In such a state will the Jews be found when they shall hear the universal call, and believe in Christ Jesus. Indeed, this is the general state of the Jews in the present day; except a Jew that are called Jews, who are very rich; and who believe just as much in the God of Jacob, as they do in Jesus Christ.
